opportunities.title: The CSO Predicted His Own $6.3B Hack — And Nobody Listened
opportunities.why_now: Binance's own security chief described the exact attack vector months before the $6.3B breach happened, and the receipts are public now.
opportunities.angle: Forensic timeline piece pairing the CSO's old quotes against the attack post-mortem — 'read the warning, then watch it happen anyway'

opportunities.title: Across Protocol's Domain Got Hijacked, Wallets Got Drained, and the Warning Came Too Late
opportunities.why_now: Across went from 'avoid the app' to 'hackers control our domain' to 'restored' in 48 hours — a live case study in how fast a DNS compromise becomes a wallet-drain event.
opportunities.angle: Minute-by-minute incident breakdown with the actionable lesson: domain security is wallet security, and users had no way to know mid-attack

opportunities.title: CertiK Says Exchanges Need Hard Dollar Caps on Hot Wallets — After a $6.3B Hack Just Proved It
opportunities.why_now: CertiK's hot-wallet-cap proposal lands days after the largest exchange hack in crypto history, turning a wonky policy idea into the obvious fix nobody implemented in time.
opportunities.angle: Opinion/analysis: why this is the security equivalent of a speed limit — boring until it's the only thing that would've capped the damage

opportunities.title: Bitcoin Core Just Admitted Thousands of Nodes Would Trust Any Stranger Over Tor
opportunities.why_now: A newly disclosed Bitcoin Core bug meant nodes couldn't properly verify who they were talking to on Tor — a quiet, years-long trust failure in the network everyone assumes is bulletproof.
opportunities.angle: Explainer for the security-literate reader: what the bug actually broke, who was exposed, and why 'Bitcoin is secure' always needs an asterisk

opportunities.title: Initia Got Hacked Twice in Three Weeks — Same Chain, Same Lesson Unlearned
opportunities.why_now: A second exploit on Initia within weeks of the first is the clearest sign yet that post-hack 'we've patched it' statements are often just marketing.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition piece: compare both Initia exploits side by side and ask why the fix didn't fix anything
